Nonchalant

/non-shuh-LAHNT/ - the stress falls on LAHNT · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Nonchalant means appearing calmly unconcerned.

The bomb-disposal veteran talked about defusing mines in the same nonchalant tone most people use for grocery lists.

Worked Example

The valedictorian found out mid-shift at the diner. Her manager read the email aloud over the milkshake machine; she nodded, said 'cool,' and went back to wiping the counter — utterly nonchalant. Only her sister, watching from a corner booth, saw her squeeze the rag until her knuckles whitened.

Nonchalant is the exact word because it describes the appearance of unconcern, true or not: the whitened knuckles tell us the calm is a performance. Indifferent would claim she genuinely did not care — a very different, and here plainly false, report.

How Nonchalant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unruffled

unruffled: calm that survives a disturbance, with no claim about caring

unfazed

unfazed: not thrown off by something startling or difficult

Antonyms

flustered

flustered: visibly rattled and disorganized

jittery

jittery: twitchy with nerves

How Strong Is It? — relaxed → nonchalant → blasé

relaxed vs. nonchalant

relaxed vs. nonchalant: Relaxed just means at ease; nonchalant goes further, wearing visible unconcern about something most people would react to.

blasé vs. nonchalant

blasé vs. nonchalant: Blasé outdoes nonchalant: the nonchalant winner may be hiding a racing heart, while the blasé one has genuinely stopped being impressed by winning at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — non-

Prefix — non-: not

Root — chalant

Root — chalant: caring, heating up (French chaloir, from Latin calere, to be hot)

Put it together

Put it together: Non- (not) + chalant (heating up, caring) = not heating up. French chaloir, from Latin calere 'to be hot,' meant to be worked up about something; a nonchalant person is literally one who does not warm to the crisis — the temperature never rises.

Use the root in a new word: calorie

Use the root in a new word: calorie: The label says one granola bar packs two hundred calories of energy.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / conversational

Nonchalant reports only the surface: calm unconcern on display, whatever churns beneath. That makes it the word for cool performances — and different from its cluster-mates indifferent (the concern truly absent) and apathetic (the capacity to care gone). Casually is its adverb cousin: a nonchalant shrug is given casually.
